body:
Working entry: «Status-line interception removed — user's command untouched; no `hook statusline` arm, shell-out,
settings override, snapshot command, fake-agent modes, fixtures or log subjects; 21 relied rows» (viola-0.2.0, Epoch 2 —
The budget gate and the status line leave; id chk-tnbdlbiv). Its freight is two CARRY blocks (the `pins` view: 2 rows,
cry-dc3um6ng 249 chars, cry-hqyx2rou 665 chars), both folded below. The capability it addresses is `v2-05` («The
status-line interception removed whole»), planned and unclaimed.

viola stops intercepting the wrapped CLI's status line. A wrapped session's status line is the user's own command, run
by the CLI exactly as it is unwrapped: viola writes no status-line override, passes no `--settings` for it, records no
status-line command, has no `hook statusline` arm and runs no shell for any purpose. The ledger loses the two status-line
rows that guard the interception (`statusline-override`, `statusline-shell`; `statusline-rate-limits` already left with
chunk 2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed), leaving 21 relied rows. Everything that existed only to build, test, record,
document or log the interception leaves with it.

The phase directive's nine items are the operator's directive for this chunk (inputs#I1; source:
`~/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/phase-status-line-removed-directive.md`): scope is the route entry and its two
CARRYs as they stand, a REMOVAL — every surface that leaves (code, tests, fixtures, schemas, docs, masters' rows) and
everything that stays, with why, named here; a thing the entry does not name that would leave with it is a fork on the
card, never a silent cut; every coordinate re-tested. The pinned product binary driving this session
(`~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola`, `~/.viola/bin/0.1.0-…`) and the live home `~/.viola/` are not touched — no
install, no re-pin, no write under `~/.viola/` or to the user's `~/.claude/settings.json`; a step needing one is a named
operator step that waits. The box-only fixture CARRY needs a clean `viola verify --record`, a live `claude` start: a
named operator step waiting on a per-chunk cap, never planned as granted; no live desktop step; `claude --version` is no
live start. The host is shared with another project's mutation run: research runs no cargo build or test run but what
the plan cannot be written without, each named on the card with its wall time; a baseline entry needing a build is
fired once, never in parallel. No mutation run, local or dispatched: a guard test's one-off remove-the-guard control
goes through `gate.py control` under a kill deadline, its `case` the test's NAME alone, its entry reaching the case past
fail-fast, «holds» = that case ran and FAILED. Every statement in the plan about how a tool, a crate or the CLI behaves
is measured at P3 and cited, or marked unmeasurable; an acceptance probe over identifiers is checked at P4 against the
plan's own test cases that must spell an old word (old shapes live in fixture files outside the probed paths). A removed
field or event kind: every own-format `v` stayed 1 on the founder's ruling for the budget removal ONLY — whether this
removal takes the same exception is his fork, put on the away form's file with the measured compatibility facts (new
reader / old files; old reader / new files), and the phase stops there. A red or defect found now folds into this chunk
as an `[inferred]` item with its own acceptance; one found at P3 outside the pinned scope is a Carry-forward naming its
owner entry. The phase runs exactly as the letters say, the operator away (his forks to the away form's file), and the
P5 card carries the directive's item-9 block.

- **CARRY (cry-dc3um6ng)** — «architecture · decision/no-tmux-or-shell-dependency — the status-line shell-out leaves
  (crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs:124), census F-09 (placement provisional — the founder away; rows landing
  2026-11-13T01-15-10's route-owed.md)». [inferred] The coordinate is stale as a pointer to the shell-out: at HEAD
  7416035f, `statusline.rs:124` is inside a test (`statusline_override_is_the_pinned_path_then_hook_statusline`); the
  shell-out's own coordinates are `BIN_SH` (`statusline.rs:17`) and `shell_argv` (the test at `statusline.rs:217` reads
  `["/bin/sh", "-c", command]`), run by `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`. P3 re-reads the architecture row
  `decision/no-tmux-or-shell-dependency` and closes what it states once the shell-out is gone (no viola shell for any
  purpose). The placement is provisional on the founder's word (as written).

- **CARRY (cry-hqyx2rou)** — a box-only screen fixture (the input box's rule and prompt rows with no footer literal,
  recorded by a clean `viola verify --record`) for the fake agent to replay in CI; none was recordable while
  `statusline-rate-limits` failed on this account (`--record` writes only at 0 fail); none is hand-written (from chunk
  2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box; its P5 card's «Beyond the plan» row,
  `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-13T01-42-03-phase/p5-card-1.md`, approved by the operator's own word «yes»,
  `chunks/2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box/inputs/I6-relay-1.md.txt`). [inferred] The rate-limits row
  already left (chunk 2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed), so its stated blocker is gone; the remaining blocker is the
  recording itself, a LIVE `claude` start (directive item 3): a named operator step that waits on a per-chunk cap.
  **The chunk can close without it**: nothing else in this entry depends on the fixture — the removal is proved by the
  fake agent in CI and by the code's own tests. If the cap's word does not come, the box-only fixture stays a CARRY,
  moved by the wrap onto «Live round on the trimmed product» (the version's live round, which already holds the
  `Mcp.tools-list-1.json` re-record). Whether a `--record` run after this removal reaches 0 fail on this account is
  P3's to measure without a live start, or mark unmeasurable.

# Phase directive — «Status-line interception removed» (Epoch 2, viola-0.2.0)

1. Scope is the route entry and its two CARRYs as they stand: the user's status-line command left untouched; no
   `hook statusline` arm, shell-out, settings override, snapshot command, fake-agent modes, fixtures or log subjects;
   21 relied rows; the status-line shell-out leaves (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs:124`, census F-09);
   the box-only screen fixture CARRY. It is a REMOVAL: name at P1 every surface that leaves (code, tests, fixtures,
   schemas, docs, masters' rows) and everything that stays and why; a thing the entry does not name that would leave
   with it is a fork on the card, not a silent cut. Re-test every coordinate.
2. The PINNED product binary that drives this very session (`~/.local/viola-product/bin/viola`, `~/.viola/bin/0.1.0-…`)
   and the live home `~/.viola/` are NOT touched: no install, no re-pin, no write under `~/.viola/` or to the user's
   `~/.claude/settings.json`. A step that would need one is a NAMED operator step that waits.
3. The box-only fixture CARRY needs a clean `viola verify --record`, which is a LIVE `claude` start: it is a NAMED
   operator step that waits for a per-chunk cap, never planned as granted. Say at P1 whether the chunk can close
   without it, and what stays a CARRY if the word does not come. No live desktop step. A print-and-exit read
   (`claude --version`) is no live start.
4. The host is shared with another project's mutation run through this phase: the research runs NO cargo build and
   NO test run but what the plan cannot be written without; name each such run on the card with its wall time.
   A baseline entry that needs a build is fired once, never in parallel.
5. No mutation run, local or dispatched. A guard test carries its one-off remove-the-guard control through
   `gate.py control`, under a kill deadline; the control's `case` is the test's NAME alone and its entry reaches the
   case past fail-fast. «Holds» = that case ran and FAILED.
6. Before any statement in the plan about how a tool, a crate or the CLI BEHAVES, measure it at P3 and cite the
   measurement; a statement that cannot be measured at plan time is marked as such. An acceptance probe over
   identifiers is checked at P4 against the plan's own test cases that must spell an old word (the last chunk's
   clash): old shapes live in fixture files outside the probed paths.
7. A removed field or event kind: every own-format `v` stays 1 on the founder's ruling for the budget removal ONLY;
   whether this removal takes the same exception is a fork that is his — put it on the away form's file with the
   measured compatibility facts (new reader / old files; old reader / new files), and stop there.
8. A red or a defect found now folds into THIS chunk as an `[inferred]` item with its own acceptance; one found at P3
   outside the pinned scope is a Carry-forward naming its owner entry.
9. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. The operator is away: a fork that is his goes to the away form's file
   and the phase stops there. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the union's
   `picked {n} of {N}` per master with «by every draw» and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY row the plan cites is
   in the union or its `*-standing.md` (name each in neither); every `[RETYPED]` line and `[EVERY_ROW]` re-spawn;
   every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line, and every place a letter was wrong
   or silent. A plan that needs a new KEY of a master's keyed section, or to clear a NOT YET MEASURED piece of a mark,
   says so on the card.

# Founder forks — 2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed (phase P4, away form)

Chunk: «Status-line interception removed» (viola-0.2.0, Epoch 2). Run: `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-14T19-10-38-phase/`.
Raised under the operator's phase directive, item 7 (`inputs#I1`): «whether this removal takes the same exception is a
fork that is his — put it on the away form's file with the measured compatibility facts (new reader / old files; old
reader / new files), and stop there.» The phase stops at P4 on this file; the plan is written once the answer is
appended here.

## Q1 — Does this removal keep every own-format `v` at 1, as the budget removal did?

**What leaves an own format.** The instance snapshot's `data` loses `statusline_command` (`snapshot.json`, `v` 1). The
ledger stamps' `rows` map loses the two row ids `statusline-override` and `statusline-shell` for a version this build
stamps (`ledger/stamps.json`, `v` 1). No event kind leaves (`hook statusline` emits no event), no channel `params`
field and no `list` document field leaves. Process-log lines carry no `v` (their schema filename is their version).

**The rule as it stands** (architecture · decision/protocol-version-bump-rule): «Adding a field or event kind is
additive and needs no bump of `v`; removing a field or changing its meaning bumps `v`.» Its one except: «Removing the
budget gate's fields and event kind kept every own-format `v` at 1 (snapshot, channel params, event line, list
document); readers skip the removed keys and kind.» That except was your ruling for the budget removal only.

**Measured compatibility facts** (research of this chunk, HEAD 7416035f; `doc:2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed/research` §Measured compatibility facts):
- New reader, old snapshot: `InstanceSnapshot` has no `deny_unknown_fields` (`crates/viola-state/src/snapshot.rs`, 0
  hits), so a snapshot holding `statusline_command` reads whole; the key is skipped.
- Old (0.1.0) reader, new snapshot: at `build/viola-0.1.0` `statusline_command` is optional, so its absence alone would
  parse; but that reader requires `budget_paused`, which this branch stopped writing at the budget removal, so it
  already replays every snapshot this branch writes. This removal changes nothing for it.
- New reader, old stamps: the verdict reads the relied rows alone, so a stamp still holding the two retired rows reads
  verified when every relied row passes (the pattern the budget removal proved for `statusline-rate-limits`).
- Old (0.1.0) reader, new stamps: a version re-stamped by this build holds only its 21 rows (`merge_stamp` writes the
  run's rows alone), so a 0.1.0 reader reads it unverified — already true since the budget removal (that build stamps
  without `statusline-rate-limits`).

**Options, recommendation first:**
1. **Keep every own-format `v` at 1 (Recommended).** The except of decision/protocol-version-bump-rule widens to name
   this removal too (the snapshot's `statusline_command` and the stamps' two row ids). Why: in both directions the
   facts are the budget removal's own, unchanged — new readers skip the removed key and rows, and old readers were
   already cut off by the budget removal. A bump would add a second supported `v` to the snapshot envelope and the
   stamps reader for no reader it protects. Trade-off: the rule's text gains a second named exception, and the
   «removing a field bumps `v`» rule now has two removals that did not bump it.
2. **Bump `v` by the rule as written** — the snapshot envelope to `v` 2 (and the stamps envelope to `v` 2). Every
   reader before the bump then treats a new snapshot as unsupported and replays the log (no endpoint, so an older
   client reads the instance unreachable), and treats new stamps as malformed (unverified). New readers must accept
   `v` 1 and `v` 2 alike (contract/snapshot-envelope/v: «above 1 is unsupported»; contract/ledger-stamps). Why not
   recommended: it costs a reader change and a contract change in two envelopes to protect no reader that is not
   already cut off.
3. **Bump only the snapshot envelope, keep stamps at `v` 1** — the stamps' rows map is keyed data, not a fixed field
   (one could hold the map's keys outside the rule). Same snapshot cost as option 2; stamps unchanged.

**The answer:** _(appended here, verbatim, with who gave it and when)_

### The operator's message (session, 2026-11-14)

> Answer to the fork in founder-forks.md: option 1, keep every own-format `v` at 1 — a delegate answer, PROVISIONAL,
> the rule's exception escalated at the wrap for his own word. Read
> ~/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/relay-status-line-q1.md whole, append it under the fork and snap it, then
> resume the phase at P4 and run it to the P5 card as the skill says. No cargo build or test run but what the plan
> cannot be written without (the host is shared); name each on the card.

### The relay, whole (`~/dev/projects/additional/viola-overseer/relay-status-line-q1.md`)

# Phase of 2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed — the answer to founder-forks.md's fork (a delegate's answer, PROVISIONAL)

**Option 1 — keep every own-format `v` at 1.** PROVISIONAL: the driving overseer answers as the delegate while the
operator is away; his own word ratifies or changes it, and the question is on his list for his next look.

Why this one while he is away: it is the option that stays open (a `v` written as 2 cannot be taken back without a
second break; a bump added later is additive), and it is the answer he gave for the budget removal on the same
measured facts — but his ruling was for that removal only, so this one is not settled by it.

What it binds in the plan: the measured compatibility facts stated as measured, with a test for each direction the
tree can run (a new reader over a snapshot that still holds `statusline_command`; a stamp that still holds the two
retired rows), the old shapes in fixture files outside any identifier probe's paths; the exception to
`architecture · decision/protocol-version-bump-rule` an EXPECTED AMENDMENT FOR THE WRAP, PROVISIONAL, on the wrap's
card for his own word; the steps a bump would add listed on the P5 card, so a change of his word is a cheap revision.

The `workspace.repo` exception rows that die with the status-line fixtures: put their retirement on the P5 card as a
row of its own (the entry does not name them).

event, which exits 0 silently); the `/bin/sh -c` shell-out leaves, so viola runs no shell for any purpose; `viola
verify` drops Run B's status-line probe and the two ledger rows it fed, so the relied set is 21 rows. The fake agent's
status-line modes, the harness's `boot --statusline-echo`, the `StatusLine` fixtures and schema, the fuzz seeds and
the log words leave with them (scope; `architecture · decision/no-tmux-or-shell-dependency`, whose one exception
`architecture · decision/no-shell-out` goes; census F-09, cap v2-05).

The removal keeps every own-format `v` at 1, on a delegate's PROVISIONAL answer (`inputs#I2`, option 1): the snapshot
drops `statusline_command` and the stamps drop two row ids, with readers on both sides proved by tests over the 0.1.0
shapes kept in `fixtures/viola-0.1.0/`, outside the identifier probe's paths (`test-plan ·
decision/retired-words-as-fixtures`). `--settings` stays a flag of the agent crate — Runs C and D still pass it — and
moves to the crate root beside `--plugin-dir` (`architecture · decision/claude-flag-literals-in-agent-crate`). No live
step: the box-only screen fixture CARRY is a named operator step that waits on a per-chunk cap (`inputs#I1` item 3),
and the chunk closes without it.

1. **The agent crate** (`crates/viola-agent-claude/`): delete `src/statusline.rs` and `pub mod statusline`
   (`lib.rs:10`); add `pub const SETTINGS_FLAG: &str = "--settings";` to `lib.rs` beside `PLUGIN_DIR_FLAG` (:83), with
   a doc line naming its callers (verify's Runs C and D). In `ledger.rs`: `ALL` becomes `[Self; 21]` without
   `StatusLineOverride` / `StatusLineShell` (their ids and words go); `ShellVerdict`, `StatusLineCapture`,
   `statusline_variants`, `STATUSLINE_DEFAULT`, the statusline probe checks in `check` and the `StatusLine.<k>` file-name
   helpers leave. Tests: the eight statusline cases of `ledger/test_cases_runs.rs` and the helpers of
   `ledger/test_cases.rs` (`clean_statusline`, `statusline_check`) leave; in `ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` the relied
   count reads 21 (:70), `[true; 23]` reads `[true; 21]` (:192), `verified_reads_a_failed_statusline_row_by_the_relied_set`
   leaves, the budget retired-row case's `rows.len()` reads 22, and one new case
   `verified_reads_a_stamp_holding_the_status_line_rows_on_the_relied_rows_alone` reads the two retired ids from
   `fixtures/viola-0.1.0/retired-words.json` (step 3), asserts neither is in `LedgerRow::ALL`, stamps every relied row
   `pass` with both retired ids `fail`, and reads `Ok(true)`; one new case `relied_rows_hold_no_status_line_row` asserts
   `relied()` holds 21 ids, none of the fixture's two. Keeps tests S1, S4.

2. **The state crate** (`crates/viola-state/`): `InstanceSnapshot` loses `statusline_command` (`snapshot.rs:61–64`);
   every constructor literal `statusline_command: None` goes (`board.rs`, `liveness.rs`, `replay.rs`, `strict.rs`); the
   two snapshot tests on the field (:332–369) leave; the budget test's `every.statusline_command` line (:234) goes. New
   cases in `snapshot.rs`: `snapshot_of_a_status_line_era_writer_reads_whole_skipping_its_command` reads
   `fixtures/viola-0.1.0/snapshot.json` (which holds a `statusline_command`, step 3) through the reader and gets every
   other field; `snapshot_written_holds_no_status_line_key` writes a full snapshot and asserts the file holds none of the
   fixture's snapshot key. `board.rs`'s secret test drops its `statusline_command` literal (:391) and the word
   `statusline` from its forbidden list (:784). `tests/state_replay.rs` loses `statusline_command_of` and its asserts.
   Keeps tests S1, S4, S6.

3. **The 0.1.0 fixtures** (`fixtures/viola-0.1.0/`): `retired-words.json` gains, beside the budget keys left as they
   stand, `statusline_snapshot_key` (`statusline_command`), `statusline_ledger_rows` (the two ids),
   `statusline_hook_word` (`statusline`), `statusline_source_file` (`statusline-source.json`) and
   `statusline_diag_subject` (`statusline-shell`); `snapshot.json` gains a `statusline_command` of synthetic text with no
   path, user or email (`echo viola-fake-statusline`), as a 0.1.0 start wrote it. Both stay under the fixture hygiene walk
   (`security-plan · decision/viola-format-fixtures-hygiene`). Keeps tests S6.

4. **The hook** (`src/cmd/hook.rs`, `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`): delete `hook/statusline.rs`; drop `mod statusline`,
   the `statusline::WORD` branch ahead of the event map (:89–95), `STATUSLINE_DEADLINE` (:62–64) and its test (:716),
   the `--shell` argument (:49), `capture_statusline` (:447–480) and its four tests (:1525–1603), the `BIN_SH` /
   `ShellVerdict` / capture-name imports, and the snapshot literals (:670, :907, :1134, :1652). `canonical` / `trusted`
   stay for the event and dialog paths, their order unchanged (`security-plan · decision/hook-instance-check-first`).
   The word `statusline` then maps to no event and takes the unknown-event exit: 0, nothing written, nothing read
   (`security-plan · decision/hook-unknown-event-silent-exit`). `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/hook.rs:361`'s negative
   case keeps refusing the word, read from the fixture's `statusline_hook_word`. New case in `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`:
   `hook_statusline_word_is_an_unknown_event_and_writes_nothing` — in a stamped, wrapped home, `viola hook statusline`
   with a status-line payload on stdin exits 0 with empty stdout and stderr, writes no line under `diagnostics/` and
   leaves the home's tree byte-equal; the word taken from the fixture. The two `hook statusline --capture` cases (:565,
   :569, :616) and the snapshot literal (:228) leave. Keeps tests S1, S2, S4.

5. **The start** (`src/cmd/run.rs`, `src/run/mod.rs`, `src/cmd/revive.rs`): `run` reads no status-line source
   (`STATUSLINE_SOURCE`, `statusline_source`, `statusline_command` :494–530 go), writes no `settings.json` override
   (:533–545 go) and records no command in the snapshot (:274–349, :548–579); their unit tests (:1165–1411) leave or
   lose the field. `ChildLaunch` takes no settings path: its args are `--plugin-dir <dir>` then the caller's args
   (`src/run/mod.rs:145–156`); the `SETTINGS_FLAG` import goes. New unit case in `src/run/mod.rs`:
   `child_launch_passes_no_settings_flag` — the args equal exactly `["--plugin-dir", <dir>, <user args…>]` and hold no
   `--settings`. A revived start shares this (the snapshot literal at `revive.rs:540` goes). A `settings.json` an older
   build left in an instance directory is read by nothing and passed to no child; the start neither reads nor removes
   it. New case in `tests/cli_instance_state.rs`: `run_writes_no_settings_file_in_the_instance_dir` — after a stamped
   start over the fake agent, the instance directory holds no `settings.json` and the snapshot no
   `statusline_command`. `run_rewrites_the_settings_override_each_start`,
   `run_records_the_statusline_command_of_the_home_s_source` and `path6_wrapped_statusline_prints_the_user_output_unchanged`
   leave. `tests/path1_run_start.rs`'s refused-start case drops its `settings.json` sentinel (:135–141, :176): the plugin
   files stay the start's code-bearing rewrite. Keeps tests S1, S2, S3, S4.

6. **verify** (`src/cmd/verify.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`): Run B passes no
   `--settings` (`trusted_args` :95–104 pushes `--plugin-dir` only; `Inputs::statusline_settings` goes,
   `typed.rs:46–54`); the probe dir's `typed/statusline/` and its probe settings (`statusline_captures`,
   `statusline_settings` :360–366), `read_statusline` (:443) and the `--record` status-line variants (:555) leave, with
   their tests (:733–770); Runs C and D read `SETTINGS_FLAG` from the crate root. The step-line test (:700–719) reads
   21 results, the rows after `paste-newline` renumbered `[19/21] resume-session` … `[21/21] local-command-compact`.
   Run B keeps its pastes and its one `claude agents --json` read; verify's spawn-pair count is unchanged (eight).
   Keeps layouts S1, S2; design S1; tests S4.

7. **The version gate** (`src/run/version_gate.rs`): its tests drop the statusline row group (:355–357, :389) and
   state the older-stamp sets by the 21-row relied set; comments naming the statusline rows are reworded.

8. **The fake agent** (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/`): delete `statusline.rs`; drop the
   `BIN_SH` and `STATUSLINE_DEFAULT` imports, the `statusline-echo` mode word, `--statusline-stdin`,
   `run_statusline` / `replay_statusline` and their calls (:961–962). `--settings <file>` stays accepted (Runs C and D
   pass it) and its value is consumed and ignored, so no unread field is left. Tests: the five statusline cases of
   `test_cases_modes.rs`, the three of `test_cases_opts.rs` and the `statusline_replayed` helper of `test_cases.rs`
   leave. The `agents` mode word stays.

9. **The harness** (`crates/viola-e2e/`): `boot --statusline-echo` leaves (`viola-harness.rs` with its two tests,
   `harness/boot.rs` `plant_statusline_echo` / `statusline_echo_command` and its test, `harness/session.rs` and the
   `statusline_echo: false` literals in `run/perf.rs`, `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/harness_lifecycle.rs`); `harness/run.rs`'s
   `LEDGER_ROWS` and `LIVE_PASS` read 21 rows ending `[21/21] local-command-compact`, summary
   `stamped 2.1.287  21 pass  0 fail`, its count test at 21. Keeps tests S4, S5.

10. **Schemas** (`schemas/`): delete `claude-statusline-fixture.v1.json`; `diag-line.v1.json` drops the `subject` word
    `statusline-shell`, the `hook_event` word `statusline` and the field `shell_exit_status`, each with every per-event
    list that names it (`obs-plan · decision/unemittable-schema-words-removed`); `deadline` and `deadline_hit` stay (the
    dialog path writes them: `src/cmd/hook.rs:303`, `src/run/dialog.rs:337`).

11. **Fixtures and seeds**: delete `fixtures/claude/2.1.287/StatusLine.default-1.json`,
    `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/StatusLine.default-1.json`, `fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin/statusline-absent` and
    `fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin/statusline-epoch` (the `hook_stdin` corpus 12 → 10 seeds, `ls fuzz/corpus/hook_stdin | wc
    -l`; the hook stdin parser keeps its target, `security-plan · decision/parser-fuzz-scope`).

12. **Tests and their censuses**: delete `tests/hook_statusline.rs` and `tests/support/statusline.rs`; drop its
    `[[test]]` (`Cargo.toml:117–118`), its `binary(hook_statusline)` term on the ci kill-line filter
    (`.config/nextest.toml:24`) and `mod statusline` (`tests/support/mod.rs`); `tests/cli_links.rs` takes `CANARY` from
    `support::verify` (the same value, `tests/support/verify.rs:24`). `tests/support/home.rs` loses
    `plant_statusline_source`, `statusline_marker`, `statusline_echo_command`; `tests/support/fake.rs` loses
    `wait_statusline`; `tests/support/verify.rs` loses the `StatusLine` variant row (:110). The censuses follow the code:
    `contract_bounded_readers.rs`'s `BOUNDARIES` loses the source read, the arm's stdin and the shell-out stdout rows
    and their witnesses; `contract_os_gated_tests.rs`'s `GATES` loses every row naming a removed case (:36 and its
    kin); `contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` loses the statusline schema walk and its planted cases; `contract_fake_agent_drift.rs`
    loses the statusline replay drift cases; `contract_diag_schema.rs` loses the removed schema words; `contract_ledger_probes.rs`
    `ROW_IDS` at 21 and its summary `21 pass  0 fail`; `tests/cli_verify.rs` `STEPS_PASS`, `ROW_IDS`, `STAMPED_PASS` at
    21; `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs`'s no-framing case loses the two statusline rows; `tests/cli_verify/stamps.rs` states
    its stamp sets by 21; `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` loses its three statusline cases; `tests/security_negatives_strict_modes.rs`
    loses the `StatusLine` arm of its payload table; `tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs` loses the snapshot
    literal; `tests/tui_passthrough.rs` loses `passthrough_with_a_statusline_source_adds_no_viola_bytes` (the unwrapped
    byte comparison stays the zero-viola-bytes guard, `a11y-plan · decision/zero-viola-bytes-on-the-terminal`); the
    other snapshot literals go (`src/run/{dialog,send/slot,wheel}.rs`, `crates/viola-mcp/tests/handlers.rs`).
    Keeps tests S1–S5; obs S1, S2; a11y S1–S4.

13. **The identifier sweep**: every comment, doc line and literal in `src crates tests schemas fuzz/fuzz_targets
    Cargo.toml .config` that spells a status-line identifier is removed or reworded, so the first probe of the block
    exits 1 with no output; a case that must still spell an old word reads it from `fixtures/viola-0.1.0/retired-words.json`
    (steps 1, 2, 4).

14. **No control is owed.** The chunk adds no product guard a remove-the-guard edit could neutralise: the hook's
    unknown-event exit and the snapshot reader's tolerance of an unknown key stand at HEAD and are not this chunk's
    code; the new cases are absence and compatibility witnesses. No mutation run, local or dispatched (`inputs#I1`
    item 5).
- none

- The 70 items of research.md's «Files to modify» (`doc:2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed/research`), read by
  `gate.py scope`: deletions marked there (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/statusline.rs`, `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`,
  `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/statusline.rs`, the two `StatusLine.default-1.json`, the two `hook_stdin` seeds,
  `schemas/claude-statusline-fixture.v1.json`, `tests/hook_statusline.rs`, `tests/support/statusline.rs`), every other
  file changed as its line says.

No live step: no `claude` start, no desktop step, no install or re-pin, nothing written under `~/.viola/` or to
`~/.claude/settings.json` (`inputs#I1` items 2–3); the fake agent carries every leg. No mutation run and no control
(step 14; `inputs#I1` item 5). The diff deletes fixtures, a schema, fuzz seeds and a test binary and changes the diag
schema, so the hygiene and CI entries stand; the one CI leg is `ubuntu-latest`, and no OS-conditional site is added (the
statusline gates removed were unconditional since chunk 2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci). The smoke boot reads a
start that writes no settings override. Entries byte-equal to the previous chunk's keep its recorded greens; the new
cargo entries are fired once each at P5, one after another, never in parallel (`inputs#I1` item 4).

  child no `--settings` (`child_launch_passes_no_settings_flag`) and writes no `settings.json` in its instance directory

  exactly as unwrapped — viola writes nothing under `~/.claude` and adds no settings layer (by construction:

  and writes nothing (`hook_statusline_word_is_an_unknown_event_and_writes_nothing`); the identifier probe

  is 21 rows, none a status-line row (`relied_rows_hold_no_status_line_row`, `contract_ledger_probes`). (per census

body:
## 2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed — Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these): 1 row(s)
**Section:** Security Anti-Patterns (NEVER do these)
**Change:** ~ decision/absolute-viola-path-in-commands · name: was «Hook, MCP and statusline commands use an absolute viola path»; now «Hook and MCP commands use an absolute viola path»
**Why:** decision/absolute-viola-path-in-commands: The cascade sweep found the name still naming statusline commands; no statusline command is written any more (Retired (1)), and the rule set at tx 1287 already names hooks and MCP alone.
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-15T05-56-26-wrap/

- Every time bound viola holds (wait timeout and cap, dialog hold, send readiness gate, confirmation windows, agents read) falls on the driver or viola's child; no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. The one `claude agents --json` read `viola list` and `viola revive` each make (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is killed at 5 s, a bound on viola's own child only: a failed, oversize, malformed or timed-out read fails open, and no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it. `viola wait` returns `{timed_out:true}` only for a timeout the caller passes in. The MCP `wait` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) clamps its `timeout_ms` to `WAIT_CAP` 50 000 ms, also its default when the caller passes none (`viola_mcp::wait_timeout`), so an MCP `wait` with no timeout is answered `timed-out` after 50 s: a bound on the driver only (the hidden, plugin-run `viola mcp` serves a driving Claude session, never a person), no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it, and the wheel is untouched. A raised dialog takes a `viola answer` only within the dialog hold (`config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`, whole seconds 60–3600, default 60, PROVISIONAL bounds; chunk 2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver); at the hold's end the wrapper replies `null` and appends one `dialog-expired` line, the dialog renders for the human in the `claude` TUI, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` / `unknown-dialog` (exit 13) — the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed; a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`. Once typed, a confirmed `viola send` waits for its confirmation within `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s), and a `/compact` send on a verified CLI within its own `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL, architecture [Delivery Confirmation]); a send not confirmed inside its window is `not-delivered` / `no-prompt-submitted`: a bound on the driver only, the confirm wait takes no key and blocks, refuses or delays none, and the wheel is untouched.

- Precedence: CLI flags > `<viola home>/config.json` > built-in defaults. Home resolution: `--home` → grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR` → `~/.viola/` (as landed, `hook` and every CLI verb, `run` and `revive` included, take `--home`, else the `VIOLA_DIR` grandparent when `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` pass `instance_of`'s shape check (a failing pair falls through to the default, never refusing), else the default; a home that exists is canonicalised; `viola hook`'s event and dialog paths take the `instance_of` session only when its `VIOLA_DIR` instance directory exists and passes `check_instance`, else exit 0 with no `config.json` read, no stdin read, no line and no frame).

- No status-line interception: no settings layer, no `--settings` at start, no `statusLine` source read and no status-line command run; the crate still holds the `--settings` flag (`SETTINGS_FLAG`) that `viola verify` reads, and the stamps no longer carry the two status-line row ids.

- Ledger rows (S3, S7, S8, R8 identity floor, shim resolution, harness prefixes, `<pasted_content>` wrapper, modal / input-box signatures, hook tier map, turn end without Stop, dialog concurrency, `claude agents --json` join field (row `agents-join` since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board: both `pid` and `sessionId` exposed, relied on every build), local commands + post-conditions, tag escaping, largest hook payload) are compiled here, never built from runtime or upstream text.

- `ledger` module (as landed, pure, no I/O): `LedgerRow`, twenty-one closed rows (the members of `LedgerRow::ALL`, in its order) `shim-resolution` · `spine-hooks` · `session-start-fields` · `prompt-verbatim` · `stop-message` · `largest-hook-payload` · `modal-signature` · `input-box-signature` · `quiet-period` · `confirm-window` · `question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency` · `long-paste-wrapper` · `tag-escaping` · `local-command-clear` · `paste-newline` · `resume-session` · `agents-join` · `local-command-compact`; the relied set `LedgerRow::relied()` (every row of `ALL`, in its order, all twenty-one); (no status-line capture, variant or shell verdict: viola intercepts no status line);`resume_target` (Run E's target id: the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture, only when `is_session_id` accepts it) and `resume_variants` (`SessionStart.resume-1.json`); `AgentsCapture` / `agents_variant` (Run B's agents capture and its `Agents.recorded-1.json` filter); `TypedRun`, `Probes { print, typed, trusted, dialogs, resumed, agents }` (`trusted`: Run B's captures in claim order; `resumed`: Run E's captures in claim order; `agents`: Run B's one agents capture, an `AgentsCapture`, on which `agents-join` passes only when it parses and holds exactly one row whose `pid` is Run B's child pid, whose `sessionId` is the `session_id` of Run B's first SessionStart capture and whose status is idle or busy (`agents_joined`), and fails with no capture; the `local-command-compact` row passes only when the first SessionStart capture of source `compact` after the newline turn's prompt (`compact_start`) has a non-empty `session_id` equal to that of Run B's first SessionStart capture, no UserPromptSubmit carries `/compact`, and `compact_latency_ms` is within `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (`local_command_compacted`)); Run B's six compiled paste texts (`PROBE_PROMPT`, `PROBE_NEWLINE_PASTE` (113 bytes, ASCII, exactly one LF at neither end, no CR) and `PROBE_COMPACT_COMMAND` (the list's `/compact`) among them); `FRAMING_TURNS` (in paste order `paste-1` · `paste-2` · `paste-3` · `compact-1` · `clear-1`) and `framing_stem`; `CAPTURE_EVENTS`; `parse_version` (first line exactly `X.Y.Z (Claude Code)`); `capture_plugin_files` (plugin `viola-verify-probe`, four exec-form `--capture` hooks); `check(row, &Probes)`, `largest`; `merge_stamp` (writes `measured.typed_probe`), `verified` (every row of `LedgerRow::relied()` `pass`, all twenty-one on every build, a stamp holding a retired ledger row verifying on the relied rows alone; a stamp holding exactly the seventeen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row holds, or exactly the eighteen ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-one ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows holds, or exactly the twenty-two ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board holds, or exactly the twenty-three ids every stamp written before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row holds, all `pass`, reads unverified; so every home stamped before chunk 2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify`); `scrub`, `is_clean` (reads through `unclean`), `signature_rows`, `screen_is_clean`, `screen_fault` → `ScreenFault { row, seam, why }`, `unclean` → the closed `Unclean` codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`. `verified` returns `Result<bool, AgentError>`: a wrong-shaped envelope is `AgentError::StampsMalformed` ("the capability stamps are malformed"). `AgentError` sits at the crate root and also holds `resolve_program`'s one refusal, `ProgramNotFound`, with a fixed message (arch [Error Handling]). `resolve_program` returns `Result<PathBuf, AgentError>`, in the crate and in the root wrapper `src/run/mod.rs`.
- **Ledger rows + probes, screen signatures, agents parser:** same crate
- **Property / fuzz:** hook stdin, `claude agents --json`, vt100 under `catch_unwind`, `prompt-submitted` normalisation

Everything on disk: viola home resolution (`--home` → grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR` → `~/.viola/`; as landed (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract) `hook` and every CLI verb, `run` and `revive` included, take the `VIOLA_DIR` step through the root bin's `resolve_home` / `resolved_home` (`src/cmd/mod.rs`), only when `VIOLA_NAME` and `VIOLA_DIR` pass `instance_of`'s shape check, a failing pair falling through to the default, never refusing; `viola mcp` resolves its home through the same `resolved_home`), ndjson append logs (one `write` per line), atomic JSON snapshots (tempfile `persist` through the one helper `fs::replace_private` / `replace_private_shared`), std `File::lock` on `.lock` siblings (opened for write), the `events.ndjson` reader `events::read_from` (each line under `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` with its start and end offsets; per-read counts `unknown_kinds` · `unknown_fields` · `torn_lines`; a line of an unknown kind is not returned; an over-long line, a non-object line and the unterminated last line count as torn, the last neither returned nor rewritten), the healing append (an append to a log whose last byte is not LF writes one LF and its line in one write, then logs `state-recovered`), liveness (heartbeat + sysinfo pid/start time; `liveness::start_times`, one process-table read; `liveness::live_endpoint(instance_dir)` → `Option<LiveEndpoint>` (`{ endpoint, pid, started_at }`, all from its one `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` call and only on a real snapshot: a replayed or absent one, or a failed read, gives `None`), shared by CLI `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` / `link` / `unlink` and `viola-mcp`'s frame tools, and giving none for a stale wrapper too; `liveness::without_endpoint(instance_dir)` → `UnreachableCause`, where `live_endpoint` gives none: read through `symlink_metadata`, a directory is `InstanceDead`, anything else (absent, a regular file, a symlink) `UnwrappedName`, opening nothing and writing no line, behind the strict-modes check at both callers, `client::Unreachable::without_endpoint` and `viola-mcp`'s `frame`; the server identity check (the closed `ServerVerdict` `Matches` · `Mismatch` · `Unverifiable`, the pure `server_verdict`, the joined `verify_server` reading the observed start time through `process_start_time`: the snapshot's pid and start time against the connected server's, made before the first frame by those CLI verbs, `viola hook` and `viola-mcp`'s frame tools; with no peer pid reported, `Unverifiable`, no frame written)), the classified snapshot read (`snapshot::read_snapshot_classified`) and the log replay (`replay`: library code, read through `read_snapshot_or_replay` by five product readers, each after the instance's strict-modes check: `viola revive`'s preflight (one read for both its collision check and its recorded directory), `viola list`'s `board::read`, `liveness::live_endpoint`, `viola hook`'s `connect` and `run`'s collision check; no product code under `src/` calls `read_snapshot`; `replay::session_chain` gives one link per `session-start` line with a string id, with the pass's skip counts, and writes and logs nothing), the optional snapshot field `cwd` (the start's spawn directory; no event carries it, so a replay gives none), the instance check `strict::check_instance` (the home (the read rule), `instances/` (the write rule), the instance directory (the read rule), its `diagnostics/` (the read rule), its `snapshot.json` (the write rule) and its `events.ndjson` (the write rule), each that exists, a folder before what it holds), `ledger/stamps.json` reads (`config.json` is read by the root bin, `run::dialog::read_hold`, not here), and the home strict-modes check (Unix owner + modes) with 0700/0600 creation, in two rules — the write rule, and the read rule (`unix_read_verdict`: no group or other bit) —, and beside `check_instance` the checks `check_home_tree(home, name, key)` (the home; with a name `check_instance`'s set; `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`; with a key `bin/<key>/`, the pinned `viola`, `plugin/<key>/`, its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`; each that exists; refusing as `TreeRefused::HomeLevel` or `TreeRefused::InstanceLevel`; called by `run`'s and `revive`'s starts and by `verify` with no name and no key), `check_diagnostics` (a symbolic link refused; run by `open_role_file` / `write_detail` before anything is narrowed), `check_stamps` and `check_socket_dir` (one `symlink_metadata`: an absent path passes, an unstattable one is `Refused::Unreadable`, then `socket_dir_verdict` reads a symlink as `Refused::Symlink`, a non-directory as the fixed-message `Refused::NotADirectory` and anything else by the read rule; it never chmods, a refused directory stays as found), with `check_endpoint_dir`, that check on a recorded endpoint's parent, run before a bind (`viola run`, `revive`'s start) and before each client's connect (the CLI frame verbs, `hook`, `viola-mcp`'s `frame`).

- Strict-modes runs in every process that reads `snapshot.json` or `ledger/stamps.json` (`run`'s and `revive`'s starts and `verify` through `check_home_tree`, `verify`'s `update_stamps` through `check_stamps`, `run`'s version gate through `stamps::read_stamps_strict` (the `strict` module's `check_stamps` first, a refusal `cli_verified:false`), `hook`'s event and dialog paths through `trusted`, the CLI frame verbs `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release` and `link` / `unlink` through `client::refuse_untrusted`, `viola mcp`'s frame tools through `check_instance`); each existing `events.ndjson` is checked before it is opened.

- Readers: over-long lines (> `MAX_FRAME`) count as `torn_lines`; unknown kinds/fields are counted in `skipped`; a reader never writes (the next append heals a torn last line). A snapshot with an unsupported `v` or a parse failure → replay (`state-recovered`) through `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, whose five product callers are `viola revive`'s preflight, `viola list`'s `board::read`, `liveness::live_endpoint`, `viola hook`'s `connect` (a replayed or absent snapshot unreachable, so the hook fails open) and `run`'s collision check (a replayed snapshot judged by the heartbeat alone); the replay writes no file and recovers `links` from the logged `link` / `unlink` lines through the public rule `replay::apply_link_line` (a pair keeps its first `since` until an `unlink`; a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`), which the root bin's `LinkSet` applies as well.

- Only the instance's wrapper writes its snapshot; only `viola verify` writes stamps; no process writes or reads a `budget.json` (no budget reading is kept). viola is a local-only, single-user tool: no accounts, no public listener, no database, no stored credentials and no regulated data. Its risk is the local privilege boundary. The IPC endpoint is effectively a code-execution interface (`send` types prompts, `answer` can allow PermissionRequest tool calls). Several state files decide what code runs (the plugin exec paths, the pinned binaries, the ledger stamps). The plan is a Minimal baseline with targeted elevations for each of these.

Built: the mode word `agents` (a first word `agents` answers `agents --json` from files beside its exe: `agents-mode` (`recorded` · `oversize` · `malformed`, absent = `recorded`), `agents-rows.json` (planted rows) and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry, a row written just before its launch SessionStart fires, a dead or reused pid skipped through one `viola_state::liveness::start_times()` read; built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`; no option and no env added). Exits on `\x03` or at stdin EOF, first waiting for a hook still running and starting no other; on Unix every command it spawns (each hook) runs in a process group of its own (`process_group(0)`, as the `--exit-no-eof` holder does), because a hangup of its PTY's foreground group, at its exit as session leader or when a killed wrapper closes the PTY, cuts a `viola hook` short in its exit-time coverage write (a cut-short profile, measured); the agent itself, its PTY's session leader, cannot leave that group (`setpgid` refuses a leader), so on Unix its exit ignores SIGHUP from its first step (`\x03` or stdin's end): a hangup that lands while it exits (a killed wrapper, or portable-pty's SIGHUP-first kill) no longer cuts its own exit-time coverage write, and one that lands before the exit begins still ends it (measured). That exit, shared Unix code, is witnessed on Linux only: `tests/cli_fake_agent.rs` `fake_agent_exit_outlives_a_hangup_that_lands_while_it_exits` (`cfg(target_os = "linux")`) reads the SIGHUP disposition through `ps -o sigignore= -p <pid>`; it runs on CI's one leg, `ubuntu-latest`.

- It must not drift from the recorded `viola verify` fixtures, the spine, the dialog variants, the framing variants (`paste-<n>`, `compact-<n>`, `clear-<n>`) and the resume variant (`SessionStart.resume-1.json`, by `fake_agent_resume_replay_matches_every_recorded_resume_set`) and the compact variant (`SessionStart.compact-1.json`, once resumed into its own session, by `fake_agent_compact_replay_matches_every_recorded_compact_set`), which `contract_fake_agent_drift` replays byte for byte (contract suite); it also compares the key and type shape of the fake agent's `agents` rows with each recorded `Agents.*.json` set (`fake_agent_agents_replay_matches_every_recorded_agents_set`).

- Init order: panic hook first → clap → home/instance/role → home strict-modes (create first if new) → diagnostics dir/file checks and open → `config.json` → subscriber → `process-start`. Every `viola hook` arm but the `hook <event> --capture` arm (the event and dialog paths) runs its instance check (`canonical`, then `trusted`: `check_instance`) BEFORE this init (the role-file open sets an existing home to 0700, so a check made after it passes a widened home) and a refused or absent instance (a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory included) writes no line and opens no role file (exit 0 at once; the event and dialog paths also read no stdin, send no frame and make no SessionEnd append); its stdout carries the decision body, never telemetry. Both `viola revive` arms (the start arm and `--list`) run their instance check before the log init as well: a refused check is the stderr pair, or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"strict-modes-failed","detail":null}` document, and exit 1 with no log opened. `viola link` / `viola unlink` (on `instances/<driven>`) and `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` and `release` (on their named instance; `send` after its text read) run `check_instance` on the home and the instance through the one `client::refuse_untrusted` before the log init too: a refusal is exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}` document, with no role file opened and the directory's mode left as found. `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start arm (after its instance check) run the home-tree check `strict::check_home_tree` (through `checked_exe`: the home, the `check_instance` set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned copy, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists) before the wrapper log: a refusal is exit 1 with the home pair (the instance pair for an instance-level refusal; under `viola revive --json` the `strict-modes-failed` document), no log opened, no line and no child.

- The hidden capture arm, `hook <event> --capture`, does no obs init and writes no line (a bounded panic-line exemption, obs-plan §10). `viola verify` runs `strict::check_home_tree` on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log opens: a refused tree is exit 1 with the home pair, no step line, no log and no line; a refused `update_stamps` (`StampsError::StrictModes`, nothing read or written) prints the same pair and exits 1 through its own `process-exit`, which under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` carries `detail:"strict-modes-failed"`; every other refusal past the tree check writes its own code there (`program-not-found`, `pinned-hash-mismatch`, `version-unreadable`, `unclean-fixture`), a failing row is no refusal and carries no code, and the fixture's `<file>` enters no code. A `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM (`SIGINT` / `SIGTERM`) starts no further spawn, kills and reaps the child it is running, closes every spawn pair it opened (a child of an interactive PTY run killed at the stop closes with `duration_ms` and a `child_exit_status`, the PTY pump's exit code; a print-mode or `--version` probe child killed at the stop is not measured) and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` (a member of the `process-exit` `detail` enum `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` closes at 19 values); `run`'s version gate observes no stop.

- `viola revive`'s start arm logs as process `run` once its instance check has passed (`run-<name>.ndjson`, each preflight refusal — `already-live` (a live holder or a fresh replayed beat), `stale-heartbeat` (a stale holder), `no-session`, `session-live`, `cwd-missing` — one `process-exit{exit_code:1, detail}`; its `session-live` reading, skipped under `--fork` and passing on a failed read, writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"agents-probe"}` pair there, plus one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}` on an oversize or malformed answer); `viola revive --list` is role `cli` (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract; the sixth exemption retired): after its strict-modes check passes and only under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME` it writes `process-start` / `process-exit` (`exit_code` 0 with no detail; `exit_code` 1 `detail:"no-session"` on an empty chain) into the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`, with no name no log, and its dispatch `Err` or panic reaches the `cli` catch site. A refused instance check on either `viola revive` arm (start or `--list`), or `viola mcp`'s refused `viola_state::strict::check_path` of its home or `diagnostics/` (run before its `mcp` role file opens; exit 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr), or `viola plugin install`'s refused `check_path` of its home or a `marketplace/` tree dir (run before its `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the stderr pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), or `viola link` / `viola unlink`'s refused `check_instance` of the driven instance (run before their `cli` role file opens; exit 21, the fixed instance-state pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), opens no role file and writes no line (the seventh exemption). So does a refused strict-modes check on the hook event and dialog paths (exit 0, nothing printed), on `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause` or `release` (exit 21, the instance pair or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document), on `viola verify`'s home tree (exit 1, the home pair) or on the home tree of `viola run` or `viola revive`'s start arm (exit 1, the home or the instance pair) (the eighth exemption). A refused peer euid (Unix) or a failed server check (the peer pid and start-time comparison, run on Linux, the one target) sends no frame and opens no `channel.request`: the eight CLI frame verbs (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`; `link` / `unlink` into the driven instance's `cli-<driven>.ndjson`) end `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside their dispatch span with no `channel-request` line; `viola hook` writes `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}` at WARN (on a dialog hook `hook-invoked{corr:null}` first, then `decision_emitted:false`); MCP's frame tools return `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and no line, as their refused `check_endpoint_dir` (made after `live_endpoint`) does with `detail` `socket-dir-refused` and no frame, and as the liveness pre-check's does with `without_endpoint`'s reading (`instance-dead` or `unwrapped-name`) and as their own refused `check_instance` of the home and the instance directory does (made before `live_endpoint`, `detail` `strict-modes-failed`, no frame); no pid, start time, path or endpoint in any line. A refused socket directory (`check_socket_dir`, the strict-modes read verdict) is none of these exemptions and writes under its own closed word `socket-dir-refused`, with no path, pid or uid in any line: `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start (`socket_dir_ready`, no span, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`; a failed create, a lost race and a refused check read one code, and a `Server::bind` failure is not this refusal) one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, under `viola revive --json` the same-shaped `socket-dir-refused` document; the eight CLI frame verbs one `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"socket-dir-refused", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside their dispatch span, no `channel-request` line and no frame; `viola hook` one `hook-decision{detail:"socket-dir-refused"}` at WARN inside `hook.handle` (on a dialog hook after `hook-invoked{corr:null}`, with `decision_emitted:false`), exit 0, empty streams and no frame.
